_meta.purpose: Hand-curated set of well-known paired-referent framing terms in U.S. political discourse, for S2.11 Euphemism Genealogies (docs/12 §S2). Each pair names two competing surface labels for (roughly) the same policy referent; the conventional partisan lean of each label is recorded as metadata only and is NOT used in any gate. The measurement reports the actually-observed per-party usage split per label over congress-press 2013-2026. Descriptive: the artifact is the set of per-pair splits and any crossover (label used more by the party NOT conventionally associated with it).
_meta.curation: Hand-curated from widely-documented, low-controversy public political-language pairs. These are famous framing contrasts, not novel claims. Surface forms are matched case-insensitively as substrings on lowercased statement text (so a form matches its own plural, e.g. 'estate tax' matches 'estate taxes').
_source: Frank Luntz's messaging playbook is the documented provenance for several right-side labels: 'death tax' (over 'estate/inheritance tax'), 'climate change' (recommended over 'global warming' as 'less frightening' in his 2002-era environment memo, which he later publicly recanted in 2019 Senate testimony), and 'tax relief' (over 'tax cut'). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Luntz ; https://grist.org/article/the-gops-most-famous-messaging-strategist-calls-for-climate-action/ ; https://scienceblogs.com/framing-science/2007/05/17/the-luntz-memo-and-the-framing ; https://www.salon.com/2007/01/23/luntz_4/

'Modern sporting rifle' is the firearms-industry (NSSF) trade term for AR-15-pattern rifles otherwise called 'assault weapons' by gun-restriction advocates. Source: https://www.nssf.org/msr/ ; https://congressionalsportsmen.org/policy/modern-sporting-rifle/

'Affordable Care Act' vs 'Obamacare', 'undocumented immigrant' vs 'illegal alien/immigrant', 'pro-choice' vs 'pro-life', 'gun safety' vs 'gun control', 'revenue' vs 'taxes', 'earned benefits' vs 'entitlements', 'public option' vs 'government-run healthcare' are all long-standing, widely-reported competing frames in mainstream U.S. political coverage; treated here as well-established common knowledge.
_meta.lean_legend: lean = conventional partisan association of the label (D, R, or neutral). Metadata only; the finding is whether the MEASURED split matches or crosses this.

pairs.note: Luntz-popularized 'death tax'. 'estate tax' substring also catches 'real estate tax' (minor noise).
Right label sums two surface variants.
Competing self-labels, not euphemisms for an identical referent; classic framing pair.

Counterintuitive provenance: 'climate change' was the Luntz-recommended GOP substitute for the older 'global warming'; it has since become the dominant neutral term used across the spectrum. Crossover expected.
'Obamacare' began as an R pejorative, later reclaimed by Democrats. 'ACA' initialism excluded (too broad as substring).
'gun safety' is the newer D reframe of what opponents/older usage call 'gun control'.
HIGH NOISE: 'revenue' appears in many non-tax budget/business contexts (incl. 'Internal Revenue Service'); 'taxes' is generic. Reported with a noise flag; interpret directionally only.
'earned benefits' is the D reframe of budget-speak 'entitlements'. 'entitlement' substring also catches 'sense of entitlement' (minor noise).
'modern sporting rifle' is the firearms-industry trade term; very low volume expected in press releases.
Right label ('death tax') is shared with the estate_tax pair by design of the task list; redundant but reported as its own pair.
Here the framed euphemism ('tax relief') is the RIGHT label and the plain descriptive term ('tax cut') is the LEFT.
